name: LightMem
licence: MIT (LICENSE file and GitHub API); pyproject.toml declares Apache-2.0, an inconsistency
one_line: ZJUNLP research library (ICLR 2026) that runs an Atkinson-Shiffrin pipeline: LLMLingua-2 token compression of incoming turns (sensory), attention+embedding topic segmentation into a token-capped short-term buffer, one batched LLM fact-extraction call per buffer flush, a Qdrant fact store, and an offline 'sleep-time' update pass; the repo also hosts StructMem, FluxMem and EM2Mem.

locomo.protocol: LightMem(512, 0.7): sensory buffer 512 tokens, LLMLingua-2 rate 0.7; gpt-4o-mini extractor and reader, gpt-4o-mini judge (Mem0-style 'generous' prompt), top-60 retrieved facts, cat 1-4 = 1,540 q, single run; 73.90 with qwen2.5-32b-instruct judge
locomo.source: experiments/locomo/readme.md (Results on LoCoMo table); search_locomo.py:373 skips category 5

locomo.protocol: LightMem(768, 0.8), same protocol as above; 74.35 with qwen2.5-32b judge. Best vendor number in repo for flat mode
LightMem(1024, 0.8), qwen3-30b-a3b-instruct-2507 backbone, gpt-4o-mini judge, 1,540 q

arch.truth.t: The Qdrant fact collection is the only durable store; raw turns are not persisted (only LLM-written facts), and pre-compression overwrites each message's content in place, so even the buffers hold compressed text. Sensory and short-term buffers live in process memory. Two traps: with a local path and on_disk=False (the defaults, path /tmp/qdrant) the Qdrant directory is deleted with rmtree whenever a store is constructed; and with the default index_strategy=None, offline_update inserts nothing, so extracted facts are dropped.

arch.stores.t: Qdrant (local embedded path or server) for facts; optional second Qdrant collection for StructMem summaries; 'context' strategy dumps entries to memory_entries.json. history_db_path and kv_cache_path are declared but never used.

arch.graphdb.t: graph_mem flag exists but memory/graph.py is a single class header with no body, which Python rejects (IndentationError), so enabling graph_mem fails at import time. FluxMem (separate package src/fluxmem) has its own in-process heterogeneous graph.

arch.scope.t: No user_id/agent_id anywhere in the core; isolation is one Qdrant collection (and one LightMemory instance) per user or conversation. Topic ids and the summary time pointer are module globals shared across instances in a process. Optional BoundMem tags filter at read.

write.entry.t: LightMemory.add_memory(messages, force_segment, force_extract, boundmem_tags); each message dict must carry a session time_stamp. MCP add_memory(user_input, assistant_reply, timestamp).

write.receipt.t: Synchronous call. If buffers do not overflow it returns an empty result while the turn sits only in RAM (sensory or short-term buffer); facts become durable only when a buffer flush triggers extraction and Qdrant insert inside the same call. A crash loses buffered turns.

write.roles.t: messages_use='user_only' default: only user messages are counted and shown to the extractor; assistant_only and hybrid are options. Sensory-buffer token counts and the coarse attention boundaries use user text only, while the fine boundary embeds each user+assistant pair concatenated. The LoCoMo harness maps both speakers to role 'user' with empty assistant replies.

write.firewall.t: not found; no injection or poisoning check on write. The extraction prompt asks for exhaustive extraction of everything that is not pure filler.

write.governance.t: not found: no redaction, consent, PII filter or retention policy.

segment.unit.t: Two buffers. The short-term buffer is always on: segments accumulate until the next would push it past 512 tokens (hard-coded; tiktoken count of user text), and one LLM extraction call covers every segment in the flushed buffer. With topic_segment on (opt-in), a sensory buffer first fills to max_tokens of compressed user text (512, or the LLMLingua model's max_position_embeddings when shared) and is cut into topic segments; without it, each add_memory call is one segment.

segment.rule.t: Coarse boundaries = local maxima of the normalised attention each user turn pays to the previous one (mean over LLMLingua-2 encoder layers 8-11, three edge tokens masked). Fine boundaries = adjacent-turn embedding cosine below 0.2, raised in 0.05 steps up to 0.5 until a boundary appears; a fine boundary is kept if within 3 turns of a coarse one, else all fine boundaries are used. The tail after the last boundary stays buffered unless force_segment. Off by default (topic_segment=False); on in README and LoCoMo configs.

segment.measured.t: No segment counts published; total write-side API calls on LoCoMo (10 conversations) are 415 at (512,0.7), 298 at (768,0.8), 255 at (768,0.7) with gpt-4o-mini, including update calls.

extract.calls.t: One call per short-term buffer flush (batching several topic segments, JSON mode), parallel up to 5 threads; event mode doubles it (factual + relational calls). Roughly 26-42 calls per LoCoMo conversation in the vendor tables.

extract.facts.t: Standalone facts with source_id pointing to the originating message; each becomes one MemoryEntry with timestamp, weekday, speaker and topic_id.

extract.episode.t: Flat mode has none. StructMem 'event' mode adds a second relational/emotional extraction call per buffer. The extractor output is tagged entry_type, but MemoryEntry has no entry_type field and the Qdrant payload omits it, so the factual/relational distinction is lost on insert and the summary prompt's type tags never appear in the core path.

extract.dates.t: Messages are shown to the extractor with ISO timestamp and weekday; the LoCoMo prompt asks to distinguish mention time from event time and resolve relative dates. The default generic prompt does not. Retrieval output prefixes each fact with its timestamp.
extract.dates.e: openai.py:304-311; src prompts.py:94-99 and experiments/locomo/prompts.py:38-44 (LoCoMo prompt imported by add_locomo.py:11, 295); lightmem.py:703 [read]

extract.neighbours.t: not found at write time; the extractor sees only the buffered segments. Existing memories are compared only later in the offline update.

extract.failure.t: Per-call exceptions are printed and swallowed (empty result, usage None); facts with out-of-range source_id are clamped or dropped with a log line. No retry, no dead-letter; buffered turns already flushed are lost.

graph.entities.t: not found in LightMem core (metadata_generate is described as extracting keywords and entities but the code extracts only facts).

graph.edges.t: not found in LightMem; FluxMem defines Ground/Distill/StepLink edges in its own package.

graph.communities.t: not found in LightMem core. FluxMem (separate package) Stage III clusters episodic nodes with KMeans (sklearn or a built-in fallback) and induces skills per cluster.

time.fields.t: One time per fact: time_stamp (session time plus 500 ms per message offset), float_time_stamp, weekday, session_time on the message; consolidation_time on summarised entries. No event-time or validity interval.

time.update.t: Offline only. Each entry gets an update_queue of the top 10 of 20 earlier-or-equal nearest neighbours; an LLM then decides update (merge candidate detail into the target text), delete (target conflicts with newer candidates: hard delete) or ignore, for entries whose candidate score passes the threshold (0.9 in LoCoMo, 0.8 in README). Online update is a no-op.

time.dedup.t: No write-time dedup; near-duplicates are merged only by the offline update LLM. Updated text keeps its old vector, so the index drifts from the stored text after an update.

derive.session.t: StructMem summarize(): walks unconsolidated facts in time windows (default 3,600 s), pulls 15 semantically related seed facts plus their same-timestamp siblings, writes a 200-350 word cross-event summary into a separate Qdrant collection with covered and seed entry ids, and marks covered facts consolidated. Manual call; off unless summary_retriever is set. Defects: exclude_ids filters on a payload key 'id' that is never written, so covered facts can return as seeds; the 'historical' scope builds an 'lt' range the filter builder ignores and then appends to a None must_not list.

derive.background.t: 'Sleep-time' update is two explicit calls (construct_update_queue_all_entries, offline_update_all_entries) run by the caller with thread pools of 8 and 5; no scheduler or queue. The offline_update_trigger path passes a wrong keyword and raises TypeError (open PR #80).

derive.forget.t: Only LLM-decided hard deletes on conflict; MemoryEntry has hit_time but nothing increments it; no decay.

index.embed.t: Default sentence-transformers all-MiniLM-L6-v2 (384-d) via HuggingFace; OpenAI embedder optional; StructMem results used text-embedding-3-small.

index.lexical.t: BM25 context retriever file is empty (2 bytes) while ContextRetrieverFactory maps 'BM25' to a class in it, so retrieve_strategy 'context'/'hybrid' cannot construct; examples/run_lightmem_bm25.py is also empty. The 'context' index strategy only appends entries to memory_entries.json in the working directory, and retrieve() always uses the vector path.

index.vector.t: Qdrant cosine collection; payload filters on equality and gte/lte ranges (float_time_stamp, consolidated flag). on_disk defaults to False, and a local store that is not on_disk is deleted at construction, so persistence must be switched on explicitly (the LoCoMo harness sets on_disk=True).

read.legs.t: Single dense leg: embed query, Qdrant top-k (default 10; LoCoMo harness uses top 60 by brute-force cosine over all entries); StructMem harness adds a summary leg (top 5).

read.temporal.t: Caller can pass Qdrant filters (equality, or gte/lte ranges on float_time_stamp); 'lt'/'gt' keys are silently ignored by the filter builder. No automatic temporal parsing of the query.

rank.gate.t: No score threshold or abstain at read; BoundMem tag filter is the only post-filter.

rank.agentic.t: not found in LightMem; FluxMem's run_task does retrieve-execute-refine loops for agent tasks.

answer.shape.t: retrieve() returns strings 'timestamp weekday fact'. LoCoMo harness groups retrieved facts by speaker into two blocks (plus summaries in StructMem mode) and sends one system message, temperature 0.

answer.size.t: About 2,600 prompt tokens per question on LoCoMo: 3,997,984 QA input tokens over 1,540 questions at top-60 facts (gpt-4o-mini, 512/0.7); qwen3 runs about 3,400. Full text is about 35,600 per question in the same table.
answer.size.e: experiments/locomo/readme.md Details table; README.md:420 [inferred from published totals]

answer.prompt.t: Mem0-style memory QA prompt: prioritise most recent memory on contradictions, convert relative times to absolute dates using memory timestamps, answer in under 5-6 words, step-by-step approach.

eval.best.t: Vendor: 72.99 (768,0.8) and 71.95 (512,0.7, the paper's headline configuration) with gpt-4o-mini reader and judge on 1,540 q. Independent: 79.08 on the JustMem harness with gpt-4.1-mini.

eval.outside.t: JustMem (competitor authors) ran it at 79.08 with gpt-4.1-mini, judge unpublished; the 'Harness the Memory' study (arXiv 2608.15008) includes LightMem among 52 systems. No result under a stricter judge found.

eval.models.t: Extractor and reader gpt-4o-mini or qwen3-30b-a3b-instruct-2507; judges gpt-4o-mini and qwen2.5-32b-instruct (both reported); embedder all-MiniLM-L6-v2.

eval.rigour.t: Good: category 5 excluded, two judges reported, token/call/runtime accounting per stage, baselines rerun in same harness, outputs on Google Drive, pre/post-update stores snapshotted. Weak: generous Mem0 judge prompt, single run, no variance; the shipped add_locomo.py uses rate 0.6, not the 0.7/0.8 in the tables; search_locomo.py defaults to the pre-update store and summaries are built from it (issue #81) while the README commands use post-update.

cost.write.t: Vendor LoCoMo (272 sessions, about 5.9k turns): 415 LLM calls and 997.6k tokens total at (512,0.7) including about 64k update tokens; 255-298 calls at 768-token buffers. Compression and segmentation run locally on the BERT-base LLMLingua-2 model (GPU expected).

cost.read.t: One embedding plus one reader call per question; no LLM in retrieval.

cost.where.t: LLM hosted (OpenAI, DeepSeek, OpenRouter) or local (Ollama, vLLM, Transformers); compressor, segmenter and embedder local (default device cuda).

trust.provenance.t: Each fact keeps speaker_id/name, topic_id and timestamp, but not the source message text or id (original_memory/compressed_memory fields are left empty). Summaries record covered_entry_ids and seed_entry_ids. No trust score.

trust.erasure.t: Only the Qdrant delete-by-id used by the update pass; no public delete/erase API in LightMemory or MCP; summaries that cover a deleted fact are not updated.

trust.auth.t: No authentication on the MCP server or the web console API (the console relies on CORS limited to localhost:5177 and keeps the API key in a plaintext JSON file, masked in responses). The OpenAI LLM client and the OpenAI embedder are built with httpx verify=False, disabling TLS certificate checks (the OpenRouter path does not use that client).

trust.sharing.t: not found; BoundMem tags are a soft read filter, not access control. An open issue (#86, 2026-09) reports cross-user memory poisoning in shared FluxMem/LightMem memory and asks for a private channel.

extras.t: Each message is token-classified by LLMLingua-2 (BERT-base multilingual default) and kept at rate 0.8 default (0.6 in LoCoMo script, 0.7/0.8 in published runs); re-compressed while over 512 tokens; falls back to original text on error. entropy_compress backend also exists but is not constructible (PR #74).
Segmenter reuses the compressor's LLMLingua-2 encoder and tokenizer, so compression and topic detection cost one small local model.
Update queues built by time-filtered (only earlier entries) vector search, then parallel LLM update/delete/ignore per entry; decoupled from write so online cost is extraction only.
Built-in per-stage counters for add, update, summarise and embedding calls/tokens, exposed by get_token_statistics().
Opt-in tag prefixes written into memory text and used to filter retrieved results by tag overlap (hard or soft resolution).
fastmcp server with get_timestamp, add_memory, offline_update, retrieve_memory, show_lightmem_instance; FastAPI job runner with SSE streams and React UI.

Separate async agent memory: semantic, episodic and procedural node graph, per-step retrieval and failure-driven graph repair, offline skill distillation until a PEMS metric converges (threshold 0.01). Not wired into LightMemory.

Event-centric multimodal memory for long video (EMNLP 2026): caption memory cells with OpenIE triples, a semantic graph with consolidation, dense+lexical scoring projected to 30-second windows; separate src/em2mem package and egolife experiments. Not wired into LightMemory.
memory_toolkits re-runs Mem0, A-Mem, LangMem, naive RAG and full context on LoCoMo/LongMemEval with a token monitor; superseded by the MemBase repo.

MessageNormalizer and the extraction pre-pass give each message in a session-level timestamp group a 500 ms offset, so facts from one session get a strict, sortable order without the caller supplying per-turn times.
A single user message larger than the sensory buffer is emitted as its own segment (with its paired assistant reply) instead of looping forever (fix merged in PR #66).

The extractor sees each message as '[time, weekday] n.Speaker: text' and returns facts with an integer source_id; the engine maps the id back to the message's timestamp, weekday and speaker, clamping out-of-range ids. The LLM never has to copy times or names.

LoCoMo harness appends BLIP captions as '(image description: ...)' to the turn text and the LoCoMo prompt tells the extractor to merge visual detail into the text facts rather than store separate image facts.

Memory manager backends for OpenAI, DeepSeek (thinking toggle and reasoning_effort), Ollama, vLLM server, offline vLLM and Transformers; with OPENROUTER_API_KEY set, a models list plus route='fallback' gives provider failover.

BaseMemoryConfigs defaults: pre_compress False, topic_segment False, messages_use user_only, extraction_mode flat, update offline, retrieve_strategy embedding but index_strategy None and no retriever config, so a minimal config cannot construct (issue #78, PR #84). LLMLingua defaults: BERT-base meetingbank model on cuda, rate 0.8, max_batch_size 50, max_force_token 100. Dead keys: extract_threshold, kv_cache, kv_cache_path, history_db_path.

FastAPI console runs every LightMem call (init, add, offline update) on one worker thread from a job queue, streams logs and stdout as server-sent events, allows cancelling only pending jobs, and resets LightMem's module-level topic counter and summary pointer when the instance is rebuilt.
Console chat retrieves top-k memories, lets the user tick which ones (selected_ids) go into the answer prompt, and returns both the retrieved and the used set.
LoCoMo builder copies the Qdrant store before the offline update and records entry counts before and after, so the effect of the sleep-time update can be evaluated separately.
LongMemEval runners (GPT and Qwen) retrieve top 20 and run the offline update at threshold 0.8; experiments/egolife holds the EM2Mem long-video pipeline.
LoCoMo harness can retrieve top-k per speaker instead of a combined top-k; the reported results use combined top 60.

token_economy.t: Three levers. (1) Compress before any LLM sees text: LLMLingua-2 drops 20-40% of tokens per message locally. (2) Batch extraction: turns accumulate to a 512-1,024 token sensory buffer, are cut by topic, and a 512-token short-term buffer is flushed as one JSON-mode call, so LoCoMo needs about 255-415 write calls in total versus about 5.5-19k for MemoryOS/A-Mem/Mem0 in the same table; memory construction is 0.76-1.0M tokens versus 2.9-68M for the baselines. (3) Move consolidation offline: the update pass costs only 39-64k tokens on LoCoMo with gpt-4o-mini (55-107k with qwen3) because the queue is built by vector search and only pairs above 0.9 similarity reach the LLM. Read side stays plain: top-60 single-line facts, about 2,600 prompt tokens per question (full text about 35,600). Paper abstract (arXiv 2510.18866, latest version): on LongMemEval / LoCoMo up to 7.7% / 29.3% accuracy gain, 38x / 20.9x lower total tokens, 30x / 55.5x fewer API calls; online test-time only, 106x / 117x fewer tokens and 159x / 310x fewer calls. These ratios are against the vendor's own baseline runs, including a weak Mem0 (36.49).

speed.t: Write: extraction calls run in a ThreadPoolExecutor (max 5); the LoCoMo harness processes conversations in a process pool of 5 with one API key each. Offline queue construction uses 8 threads and the update 5 threads, guarded by locks, but each entry's candidate lookup scans every other entry's queue, so the update pass is quadratic in store size; worker exceptions are never collected from executor.map. Compression, segmentation and embedding are local GPU models, so no network cost there, but each turn is embedded one at a time during segmentation and each fact is embedded and inserted one at a time (no batching). Nothing is async and add_memory blocks for the LLM call when a buffer flushes. Published runtimes on LoCoMo: 7,388-8,484 s memory construction and about 4,300 s QA in total for 10 conversations with gpt-4o-mini, versus 24k-118k s construction for MemoryOS/A-Mem/Mem0 in the same table. No per-query latency percentiles published.

keep: Local token-classifier compression (LLMLingua-2) before the extractor: cheap, model-free of the hosted LLM, and the same encoder doubles as the topic segmenter.
Buffer-and-batch extraction: segment by topic, then pack several segments into one token-capped extraction call (one call per about 500 tokens of user text rather than per turn).
Sleep-time consolidation off the write path, gated by vector similarity (only pairs above about 0.9 reach the LLM) and restricted to earlier entries, so update cost stays tiny.
Per-stage token/call/runtime accounting built into the engine, and reporting cost tables next to accuracy.
Timestamp plus weekday prefix on every retrieved fact so the reader can resolve relative dates cheaply.
avoid: Undurable receipt: turns sit in in-process buffers until a flush, global topic and summary counters are module-level, extraction errors are swallowed, and a non-on_disk local Qdrant store (the default) is deleted at construction, so a crash, failed call or restart silently loses memory.
Offline update rewrites fact text but keeps the old embedding, hard-deletes on conflict with no history, and summaries are not refreshed when covered facts change.

Declared-but-dead features: online update is a no-op, BM25/context retrieval is an empty file, graph_mem crashes, kv_cache/history_db/extract_threshold unused, offline_update_trigger raises TypeError (PR #80).
No tenant ids, auth, firewall or redaction, and TLS verification is disabled in the OpenAI client; user_only default drops everything the assistant says.

specialities.name: One small encoder for compression and segmentation
specialities.t: The LLMLingua-2 BERT-base token classifier drops 20-40% of tokens per message, and with precomp_topic_shared the same weights supply the attention maps for topic boundaries, so both write-side token cuts run on one local model before any hosted LLM call.

specialities.name: Attention-plus-embedding topic boundaries
specialities.t: Coarse cuts are local maxima of turn-to-previous-turn attention from encoder layers 8-11; fine cuts are adjacent-turn cosine dips with an adaptive threshold (0.2 rising to 0.5); fine cuts are kept only within 3 turns of a coarse cut. No LLM is used for segmentation.

specialities.name: Token-capped multi-topic extraction batches
specialities.t: Topic segments accumulate in a 512-token short-term buffer and are flushed as one JSON-mode call with '--- Topic N ---' sections, so the whole LoCoMo set needs 255-415 write-side LLM calls versus about 5.5-19k for MemoryOS/A-Mem/Mem0 in the vendor's tables.

specialities.name: Time-directed, similarity-gated sleep-time update
specialities.t: Each fact's update queue holds its top 10 of 20 nearest neighbours with earlier-or-equal timestamps; only pairs above 0.9 cosine reach the update/delete/ignore LLM, run offline in parallel. The whole LoCoMo update cost 39-64k tokens with gpt-4o-mini.

specialities.name: Timestamp-keyed event reconstruction
specialities.t: All facts extracted from one message share its millisecond timestamp, so StructMem treats the timestamp as an implicit event key: each semantically retrieved seed pulls in its same-timestamp siblings before cross-event summarisation.

specialities.name: Per-stage cost ledger in the engine
specialities.t: LightMemory counts calls and prompt/completion tokens separately for add, update and summarise, plus embedder calls, and exposes them via get_token_statistics(); the vendor publishes cost and runtime tables alongside accuracy.

specialities.name: BoundMem tags carried inside memory text
specialities.t: Optional environment tags are written as a JSON prefix inside the memory string, so they survive any store or export, are stripped before embedding and before display, and drive a hard or pluggable soft tag-overlap filter at read.
